title: fix(plugin-grid): a cancelled background import shows the rows the job committed, with Undo (objectui#11650)
body:
Fixes #11650

Clause-②: no

Session: `session_015W8GBu6sBiqus2L2xjMsAL` (dispatched by PM seat `domain:ui#1`, claim comment 5992312538).

## What changed

`packages/plugin-grid/src/ImportWizard.tsx`, one file of source.

- **The Cancel reads the job back.** `handleCancelImport` used to write a result with `importedRows: 0` right after `cancelImportJob`. It now reads the job through the data source's `getImportJobProgress`, which is the `GET /api/v1/data/import/jobs/:id` read the card names: the `@objectstack/client` `data.getImportJobProgress` fetches `{data route}/import/jobs/{id}`. The wizard reads until the outcome is final, at most `IMPORT_JOB_CANCEL_SETTLE_READS` (10) reads, the first at once and then one per poll interval (800 ms). It then shows the job's created and updated counts. No hand-rolled fetch, and no change to the cancel door or to the client's `cancelImportJob` answer.
- **One result builder and one settle rule for both paths.** `cancelledJobToImportResult` is the poll loop's old `cancelled` result, moved out of the loop. `isSettledJobRead` decides when a read is final, and `publishJobOutcome` publishes it. The poll loop and the cancel handler share all three.
- **Undo on the cancelled result.** When the settled read is undoable (`isImportJobUndoable`), the result shows an **Undo import** button. It runs the History list's own undo action: `handleUndo` moved into a module-private `useImportJobUndo` that both now use. After the undo the button gives way to "Undone".
- **onComplete once.** A run token (`jobRunRef`) lets only the first publisher for a run publish. The poll loop also returns when a Cancel landed while its read was in flight. So the two paths never both set a result or call `onComplete` twice.
- **Undo refreshes the list it changed.** After a successful undo, the shared undo action calls `notifyDataChanged({ objectName })`. That is the existing data-invalidation bus from `@object-ui/react`, which `ObjectGrid` already listens to. This is an in-place fix declared below.

Strings reused, none added: `grid.import.importCancelled`, `grid.import.createdCount`, `grid.import.updatedCount`, `grid.import.undoImport`, `grid.import.undoing`, `grid.import.undoConfirm`, `grid.import.reverted`. No export, prop, type member or i18n key is added to any `@object-ui/*` package.

## Why the first read after a cancel is not always final

In `@objectstack/rest`'s import-job routes, the cancel route writes `status: 'cancelled'` and `completed_at` to the job row itself, then answers. The worker keeps writing to its next progress boundary, 200 rows. Only then does it patch the final counts, the per-row results and, for a job it can undo, the undo log. Until that last write the job reads terminal, but its counts can still grow and `undoable` is still false. So `isSettledJobRead` takes a `cancelled` read as final only when it is undoable, or when it repeats the previous `cancelled` read's counts. `succeeded` and `failed` are written together with their final counts, so they stay final on first sight. The poll loop uses the same rule, so a job cancelled elsewhere, for example from the History list in another tab, is no longer shown short either.

**If the bound is hit** (no read settles within 10 reads, or every read fails), the result says "Import cancelled" and shows **no count**, because the wizard never read one. The old "0 imported" badge is gone from that path. `onComplete` does not fire there, as before.

## Live before / after (own backend, showcase `showcase_contact`)

Backend: objectstack `main` at `2df3d13d`, built in my own worktree, `objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh` on a private port. Console: `apps/console` vite from each objectui worktree, proxied to that backend. A Playwright run uploads a 5000-row CSV, ticks background import, clicks Run, then Cancel after 2.5 s, and then reads the job through the API.

| run | console source | result screen after Cancel | job read after the run |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | base `f1a177c` | `Import cancelled · 0 imported`, no Undo | `cancelled`, 1800 created, `undoable: true` |
| after | `d0bfaa4` | `Import cancelled · 1800 created · Undo import` | `cancelled`, 1800 created, `undoable: true` |
| final | `02d9266` | `Import cancelled · 2000 created · Undo import` | `cancelled`, 2000 created, `undoable: true` |

On the after and final runs, clicking Undo showed "Undone" and the job then read `revertedAt` set. A filtered contact read for that run's rows returned 0. The same filter returned 1800 for the before run's rows, which nobody undid. On the final run, one list read (`GET .../data/showcase_contact`) went out after the Undo click: that is the list refetch.

Direct API measurement against the same backend: six cancels of a 5000-row job, each after a 1.0 to 4.0 s delay. The cancel POST answered 5.8 to 9.4 s after it was sent. In the four sequential runs, the first read sent after the cancel answered was already `cancelled` with `undoable: true` and the final counts. In the two runs with a concurrent poller (one read every 50 ms plus the request time), no read ever showed a `cancelled` job that was not yet undoable. That was on this driver (SQLite). The window the settle rule guards is therefore a reading of the server source, not a live observation. The rule costs nothing when the first read is already undoable.

## Tests

Head `02d9266` (after the one merge of `origin/main` at `4367146`):

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-grid/`: `Test Files 186 passed (186)`, `Tests 1721 passed (1721)`. `vitest list --filesOnly` lists 186 files, the new file among them in the `dom` project.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid type-check` exits 0. It runs `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, and `--listFilesOnly` shows the test project compiles the new test file.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-grid lint`: `0 errors`. Per file, ESLint JSON reports `ImportWizard.tsx` with 10 warnings, the same 10 rules as on base, and the new test file with 0.
- Exit 0 for each of these root checks: `check:i18n-keys`, `check:i18n-dead-keys`, `check:new-line-citations`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:phantom-deps`, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` and `scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`.

New pins, in `ImportWizard.cancelCounts-11650.test.tsx` (10 tests, wizard driven end to end with real timers):

- cancel mid-run: the summary equals the settled job counts (1950 created, 50 updated, not the early 1800), Undo is offered, and `onComplete` is called once;
- the first read after the cancel is still `running`, and a later read settles;
- a job that never reads undoable is final once two `cancelled` reads agree, with no Undo;
- Undo on the result rolls the job back and reads "Undone";
- Undo on the result, and Undo from the History list, announce the change on the bus, and a failed History undo announces nothing;
- a Cancel clicked while a poll read is in flight publishes once;
- the poll loop does not take a job cancelled elsewhere as final on its first `cancelled` read;
- closing the wizard mid-run still reports the background job through `onComplete` (a behaviour on base that this change keeps);
- the bound hit: no count shown, no `onComplete`.

**Reverse verification, one-off and committed first.** `ImportWizard.tsx` was swapped for base `f1a177c` under a restore trap, with blob hashes checked: 9 of 10 red, and the close-mid-run pin green, as a must-keep pin should be. Restore was proven by blob equals HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

**Ablations**, each through `ablation-replace.mjs` with the landing and the restore proven:

- the settle rule reduced to "any terminal read is final": exactly 3 red (mid-run, never-undoable, cancelled elsewhere);
- the `notifyDataChanged` call removed: exactly the 2 bus pins red;
- the reset-token bump put back: exactly the close-mid-run pin red. The first attempt at this one was a no-op: the tool refused it because its replacement contained the anchor. It was re-run with a non-overlapping anchor.

Not run locally, left to CI: the full `pnpm test` farm, the repo-wide `pnpm lint`, and `check:eager-closure`. Consumers in `app-shell` were not re-tested: the public face of `@object-ui/plugin-grid` is byte-unchanged (no export, prop or type change).

## In-place fix, declared

Undo now calls `notifyDataChanged` for the object (the History list and the new result button share it). This round makes the cancel call `onComplete`, so the console list refetches and shows the committed rows. An Undo that left the list showing those rows after deleting them would be a stale state this change makes newly reachable. The bus's own contract asks for exactly this call: its doc comment says "Call this from every WRITE path after the mutation succeeds". The fix is one line, in the claimed file, inside the same gate family. The pins and the ablation are above.

## Behaviour changes for hosts

- `onComplete` now fires once after a user Cancel whose job reads back, with `cancelled: true` and the committed counts. In the console this refreshes the list and raises the usual import toast ("Imported 1800 rows."). Before, it fired for a cancelled job only when the poll loop itself saw it end.
- A poll loop from an earlier run no longer publishes into a newer run's screen.

## Acceptance notes (observations, not filed)

- **Server event loop during an import.** With a 5000-row job running on the SQLite showcase, every HTTP request to that server I timed took 4 to 9 s. The pre-cancel progress GET answered 4.1 to 6.4 s after it was sent (six runs), and the cancel POST 5.8 to 9.4 s. The import runner yields once per progress boundary (its `yieldToEventLoop` doc names framework#2824). These are latency readings, not a wrong answer. Carrier: none.
- **History-list undo error is cleared by its own reload.** `ImportHistoryPanel.load` sets its error to `null` at the start, and the undo's reload runs right after a failure. So a failed History undo shows its message only until the reload begins. This change keeps that behaviour: the refactor kept it byte-equivalent, and the new result-screen Undo keeps its own error. This was read from the source and not measured live. Carrier: none.
- The success result screen still offers Undo only through History. The card is about the cancel, so this is out of scope.
